name: Olives Mount Of
overview: The Mount of Olives holds significant biblical importance as the place east of Jerusalem where Jesus frequently traveled and taught, including His triumphant entry into the city (Matthew 21:1; Mark 11:1). It is also the site where Jesus ascended to heaven, marking a pivotal moment in redemptive history (Matthew 26:30; Matthew 24:3). Historically, it was known as the Mount of Corruption due to idolatrous practices in the time of Solomon (2 Kings 23:13), and it served as a route for those coming from the east (2 Samuel 15:30). These verses highlight the Mount of Olives as a place of both sorrow and salvation, deeply intertwined with the life and mission of Christ.
